references.text: God calls everyone to repentance to avoid judgment. In [ref:Esek 18:30-32|Ezekiel 18:30-32], the Lord urges the house of Israel to turn away from all their transgressions, so that iniquity will not become a stumbling block for them. God takes no pleasure in anyone's death but desires that all should repent and live. This is the same message as in Luke 13:5: Repent, or you will perish.

[ref:Luk 13:3|Luke 13:3] is the nearly identical parallel statement Jesus gives just before verse 5, following the example of the Galileans whom Pilate allowed to be killed. The message is the same: "If you do not repent, you will all perish in the same way."

In [ref:Apg 3:19|Acts 3:19], Peter calls for repentance with similar seriousness: "Repent then and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out." This reflects Jesus' warning in Luke 13:5 that repentance is necessary to avoid destruction.

[ref:2 Pet 3:9|2 Peter 3:9] emphasizes that the Lord does not want anyone to perish but desires all to come to repentance. This confirms the same perspective as Jesus' words in Luke 13:5 – God gives time for repentance, but without it, judgment comes.

In [ref:Apg 17:30|Acts 17:30], Paul proclaims that God now commands all people everywhere to repent. This universal call to repentance is the same as what Jesus stresses in Luke 13:5: "all" will perish without repentance.

In [ref:Åp 2:5|Revelation 2:5], the risen Christ warns the church in Ephesus to repent, or he will come and remove their lampstand from its place. The warning links repentance directly to judgment, just as Jesus does in Luke 13:5.

[ref:Jes 55:6-7|Isaiah 55:6-7] calls the wicked to forsake their way and turn to the Lord, for he will freely forgive. This prophetic call to repentance supports Jesus' urgent warning that without repentance, destruction awaits.

In [ref:Jer 15:7|Jeremiah 15:7], the Lord speaks of casting his people away because they did not turn from their ways. The consequence of failing to repent is destruction, which directly mirrors the warning in Luke 13:5.

In [ref:Rom 2:4-5|Romans 2:4-5], Paul explains that God's kindness leads to repentance, but those with an unrepentant heart store up wrath for the day of judgment. The connection between repentance and judgment echoes Jesus' words in Luke 13:5.
